promise: Build and query an inspectable graph of claims, evidence and relationships with source and time attached.
audience: Researchers and agents connecting evidence across documents.
trigger: Ingest, connect, trace, challenge or explore knowledge from supplied material.

modes.name: Build
modes.output: Nodes and edges with source, method and temporal provenance.

modes.name: Investigate
modes.when: A relationship, contradiction or gap needs examination.
modes.output: Paths, evidence, timeline and qualified gaps.

modes.name: Explore
modes.when: A person needs to inspect or reuse the graph.
modes.output: A self-contained viewer or portable graph export.

examples.title: Investigate two conflicting notes
examples.brief: Use Knowledge to show how two fictional project notes support or challenge the same claim. Start with deterministic ingestion or structured additions. Trace each relationship to its source and distinguish an asserted fact from a candidate contradiction. Do not configure an external provider.
examples.before: Two notes disagree, but a keyword search presents each in isolation.
examples.after: A temporal path and source-linked evidence expose the disagreement for review.
examples.why: Relationships and provenance make the conflict inspectable.

boundaries: Cooccurrence, centrality and candidate contradictions are not proof that a claim is true.

verification.name: Functional acceptance
verification.expected: Supplied fictional tasks exercise actual mechanisms and failure boundaries.
verification.evidence: 80 native tests passed after canonical distribution and test-package isolation updates.

verification.name: Native host acceptance
verification.expected: Actual provider/host/desktop/daemon/runner acceptance for the selected adapter.
verification.evidence: No live model, real desktop transaction, invitation, deployment or production data migration was performed by this functional baseline.

sources.role: Primary retained owner history, mechanisms and records; portable method consolidates the listed entry points.

consolidation: One portable method entry with mode references; original native engines, agents and records retained as optional adapters.
publication_status: Installation and evidence scopes are documented below.

marketing.headline: Follow a claim back to the evidence.
marketing.lead: For people connecting notes, documents and research. Knowledge turns supplied material into an inspectable graph, with sources and time attached, so you can trace relationships, question an apparent contradiction and see what changed.

benefits.title: Keep the source within reach
benefits.body: Carry provenance with the claim instead of relying on an answer with no path back to its inputs.

benefits.title: Explore a specific question
benefits.body: Use paths, evidence, gaps and timelines to navigate relationships rather than rereading an entire collection.

benefits.title: Keep a history of changing claims
benefits.body: Close a relation’s validity window and append its replacement instead of erasing the earlier view.

walkthrough.title: Choose the graph and input
walkthrough.detail: Use structured additions or deterministic cooccurrence ingestion without a model. Optional extraction needs a configured provider.

walkthrough.title: Inspect the relationship
walkthrough.detail: Follow a path or inspect its evidence, treating cooccurrence and candidate contradictions as signals to review.

walkthrough.title: Share an inspectable view
walkthrough.detail: Export the graph or generate its self-contained offline viewer with the sources available for inspection.

use_when: You need to trace a relationship across supplied documents.
A claim changed over time and the earlier state matters.
A team needs an offline view of a graph and its evidence.
not_for: Treating word cooccurrence as proof of a semantic relationship.
Claiming that a structural graph gap proves a scientific research gap.
marketing.quickstart_prompt: Use Knowledge to show how two fictional project notes support or challenge the same claim. Start with deterministic ingestion or structured additions. Trace each relationship to its source and distinguish an asserted fact from a candidate contradiction. Do not configure an external provider.
marketing.output_preview:
Claim: the export supports the selected format
Source A: specification, revision one
Source B: compatibility note, revision two
Relationship: candidate contradiction — needs review

Inspect: source passages, validity windows, connecting path
Decision: retain both claims until the actual export is checked
Share: self-contained graph viewer
marketing.example_note: Fictional graph investigation. The claim and notes are illustrative; no knowledge-correctness result is implied.
install_notes: Python 3.11 or later is required by the portable install/build helper. The installed method runs through your agent host.
The deterministic library and CLI use Python and SQLite without a model key.
Native package and command identity stay knowledge; optional model-backed operations need a separately configured route.
Choose KNOWLEDGE_HOME explicitly when you want a disposable test graph.
marketing.proof_summary: Native graph, storage, analysis and interface tests passed. A passing graph operation does not establish that an extracted claim or model-written answer is correct.
marketing.next_step: Start with a small source collection and one relationship you want to understand.

film.heading: Watch the graph answer back.
film.blurb: An 80-second tour, with no narration: a timeline of a plan that was replaced, an argument with the quotes for and against a claim, a vague question that gets a question back, and a live graph filling in as relations land.
film.note: Recorded from the real tool on public documents. It shows how the views work; it does not report results.
